attractions.name: Hanna Lake
attractions.description: A scenic lake surrounded by the Chiltan mountain range, popular for boating and picnics.

attractions.name: Hazarganji-Chiltan National Park
attractions.description: A national park in the mountains near Quetta, home to the rare Chiltan wild goat (markhor-like ibex).

attractions.name: Quetta Geological Museum
attractions.description: A museum showcasing minerals, fossils, and geological specimens from across Balochistan.

attractions.name: Liaquat Bazaar
attractions.description: A busy central market known for dry fruits, carpets, and traditional Balochi handicrafts.

attractions.name: Quetta Fruit Market
attractions.description: A vibrant market famous for Balochistan's renowned fresh fruit, especially apples, grapes, and pomegranates in season.

food_places.name: Balochi Sajji houses (Sariab Road area)
food_places.specialty: Traditional whole-lamb/chicken sajji roasted over open fire

food_places.name: Local dry fruit and nut stalls
food_places.specialty: Quetta is famous nationwide for its dry fruits and nuts

weather_info.climate_type: Cold semi-arid, highland climate (Quetta sits at ~1,680m elevation)
weather_info.best_time_to_visit: April to October (mild days, cool evenings)
weather_info.avoid_months: December to February (very cold, occasional snowfall)

travel_tips.tip: The Airport Road bypass helps avoid the congested Jinnah Road area when heading toward Hanna Lake or the national park.
Ride-hailing app coverage is limited compared to major cities; arranging a local taxi or driver in advance is often more reliable.
Check current travel advisories before visiting, and prefer flying over long overland routes when possible.
Pack warm clothing even outside winter, as evenings in Quetta stay cool year-round due to its high elevation.

history.founded: Historically significant as a frontier garrison town, with older settlement in the surrounding region going back centuries
history.city_history: Quetta grew in strategic importance under British colonial rule due to its location near the Bolan Pass, a historic gateway between South and Central Asia. It became the capital of Balochistan after Pakistan's independence in 1947 and remains an important military and administrative center.
history.province_history: Balochistan is Pakistan's largest province by area, historically home to various Baloch and Pashtun tribal confederacies, and was governed as British Balochistan before its princely states acceded to Pakistan between 1947 and 1948.
